question: On 21 February 2023, a year ago today, during the official mission of the Delegation for relations with Palestine, of which I – as an MEP – was a member, I was deported from Israel after having been detained at Tel Aviv Airport for several hours until the morning, when I was expelled. During that time, the Israeli authorities showed absolutely no respect for my diplomatic immunity.

Although this very serious affront to the European Parliament was denounced by both the President of the European Parliament and the European External Action Service, with a view to taking the necessary diplomatic action, it has been a year since my unjust expulsion and I have not yet received any information regarding the measures taken in relation to Israel to ensure that MEPs can access Palestine with the appropriate guarantees.

On 12 July 2023, the European Parliament adopted a recommendation on relations with the Palestinian Authority (2021/2207 (INI)), which calls for measures to ‘ensure that the Israeli authorities allow Members of the European Parliament to access the occupied Palestinian territory, including Gaza’.

What actions are being taken by the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy to follow up on that recommendation and ensure such access?
answer: The EU regretted the decision to refuse entry to Israel to the Honourable Member Ana Miranda, who was travelling as part of an official delegation of the European Parliament. Respect for all elected Honourable Members and the EU institution of the European Parliament is essential for good EU-Israel relations. The EU has continued to underline this in its contacts with the Israeli authorities and will continue defending the rights and dignity of all Honourable Members to exercise their mandate freely.
